The required checks pass: precheck (13 proof-bearing items), rendering (16 files), content policy (14 items), strict contracts (14/14), dependency levels (925 items across 60 pages), and `validate-plan`. No local suppliers or cross-batch dependencies were added.

**The dispatch still needs owner action:** the A-page claim correction left the pair’s owner scope receipt stale. Eight item decisions are current; six remain open, and the decision tool blocks recording them until the owner refreshes the pair scope. I did not write escalation or owner receipts. The report lists those six IDs and the scope hashes.

The report also records the published monodromy wording concern for owner review and a confirmed overgeneralization in Birman–Brendle §1.1, printed p. 3 (PDF page 4): the survey says an arbitrary unordered loop lifts to a loop at the original ordered tuple, which fails for nonpure loops. [Birman–Brendle, *Braids: A Survey*](https://www.math.columbia.edu/~jb/Handbook-21.pdf)
